subject: Reserved-capacity term flexibility and GPU-price sensitivity — Acme AI deal
messages:
From: Marta Silva <marta@acme.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Jae Park <jae@acme.ai>; procurement@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity + pricing sensitivity questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team found Redwood’s latency and fallback routing compelling. Before we move to internal procurement, a couple of questions on reserved capacity economics:

1) Our CFO is worried about GPU price volatility. If market GPU spot rates move up 20-30% over our commit term, what protections can Redwood offer on unit pricing?
2) We typically commit 12–18 months. Do you have a staged discount or indexation clause (e.g., floor/ceiling) you can share?
3) For sizing, I attached a rough usage profile (acme_multiprofile_sizing.xlsx) — we expect peak Q4 inference load. Can you recommend a 3-tier reserved SKU mix (low/mid/high) and a recommended commit tenor?

Procurement timeline: we need commercial terms and a draft SOW by next Tuesday to present to procurement and engineering.

Appreciate a short note on options and what approvals we’d need on your side for deeper discounts.

Best,
Marta Silva
Head of AI Platforms, Acme AI

Attachments: acme_multiprofile_sizing.xlsx
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Silva <marta@acme.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity + pricing sensitivity questions

Hi Marta — great to meet the team. Quick answers and a proposed path forward below (attaching the latest pricing brief).

High level options (tradeoff: price vs risk):
- 12-month standard commit: predictable unit price, standard 10% tiered discount on reserved SKUs; no GPU-index clause. Fastest approval path.
- 18–24 month stepped commit: higher up-front discount (15–22%) with a mid-term review at 12 months. We can add a conditional GPU-price protection band (price floor) tied to an industry index; protects Acme for a pre-agreed downside but requires Legal + Finance signoff.
- 12-month with contingency buffer: standard pricing + optional 10% burstable capacity at fixed rate (good if you want operational flexibility without re-pricing).

GPU-price sensitivity: we can offer a limited indexation clause that triggers an internal discount review if GPU market cost moves >20% vs baseline. Practically, this looks like: quarterly check, if delta >20% we (a) apply a temporary credit to unit pricing for the next quarter or (b) open a reprice corridor with a cap/ceiling. Both require CFO-level approval for deals >$2M ARR.

Recommended sizing and SKUs: based on your spreadsheet, I recommend a mix of 40% mid Sku, 40% high-SKU for inference-heavy models, and 20% low-cost background workers for embeddings/ETL. See attached 'redwood_reserved_pricing_v3.pdf' for per-SKU throughput and estimated token costs.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a one-page commercial options table (12 / 18–24 / 12+burst) today.
2) Marissa (sales ops) and Kimberly (pricing/finance) — can you confirm whether Finance will approve an indexation-triggered credit path for deals in this band (deal_id ACME-2028-Q2-42)? If not, what alt approvals are needed?
3) Marta/Procurement — if you can confirm target tenor and any internal constraints (e.g., maximum off-balance commitments), I’ll draft SOW language and submit for internal signoffs.

Thanks — attaching both the dataset you sent and our pricing brief.

—Aditya
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_reserved_pricing_v3.pdf; acme_multiprofile_sizing.xlsx

Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity + pricing sensitivity questions — need pricing/finance guidance

Forwarding Marta’s procurement note and my initial options. Key ask: can Finance sign off on a limited indexation-triggered credit (quarterly review) for this deal?

Why this is different: Acme expects a fast Q4 ramp (see attached sizing). If GPU costs spike, they want a predictable cost corridor or a temporary credit — they prefer contractual language vs ad-hoc credits.

Specifically, please advise on:
- Approval threshold: is $2M ARR the right trigger for requiring CFO/GC sign-off?
- Proposed credit mechanics: temporary quarterly credit vs direct unit price reprice (which do we prefer operationally)?
- Max discount floor we can provide without exec escalation. Our standard docs allow up to 15% via AE + Sales Ops; anything above requires sales leadership + finance approval.

Also adding Laura Bishop for visibility/expedite (she’s handling a parallel strategic commit this quarter).

Onward —
Aditya

Thanks for surfacing this, Aditya. I reviewed the sizing and the pricing brief. High level decision and guidance below so you can move to Procurement with a clear playbook.

Decision (approved path):
- Offer three options to Acme on the SOW (presented as table): 12-month standard (baseline discount), 18-month stepped (approved up to 18% discount), 24-month protected (approved up to 22% discount but requires exec sign-off and SLA commitment).
- Approve a limited indexation-trigger mechanism: quarterly market check using the agreed GPU index (we’ll share the index source in the SOW). If market costs rise >20% from baseline, apply a quarterly credit equal to (delta * reserved utilization share) capped at 10% of monthly invoice. This is a credit path (not permanent reprice) to avoid long-term P&L exposure.
- For deals >$3M ARR require Finance + Legal review; for deals $1–3M ARR, Sales Ops + Head of Pricing can approve. ACME deal estimate currently falls in $1.5–2.5M range — route to Finance if the final committed ARR exceeds $2.5M.

Operational notes:
- Pricing team will publish the index clause template by EOD tomorrow — use that language in the SOW.
- Include a 'burst fall-through' option: for the first 3 months of a spike, allow their runbook to rely on burstable capacity at pre-agreed rates (lower operational friction).

Marissa: please prepare the commercial option table with the three tenors and the cap/credit mechanics. Kimberly: please flag whether any of the proposed caps break existing discount guardrails. If so, call me directly.

Aditya — present this as a packaged set to Acme procurement; emphasize the credit is temporary and tied to utilization so we control exposure. If they push for full reprice we lean on the stepped 24-month option and exec sign-off.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
